text:
maria.l: Heads up — the PTQ canary (raven-lite-v2 int8 PTQ) is showing a 3x uptick in funcall/structured-output parse failures compared to fp16. Quick numbers: funcall_parse_fail_rate went 0.6% -> 1.9% over the last 2h.

yasmin: Can you paste an example of the broken output? streaming or non-streaming?

maria.l: Streaming. Sample payload we hit in unit test:```
{
  "action": "create_ticket",
  "params": {
    "title": "Payment error",
    "body": "User sees error code 502
    --
    "
  }
}
``` The model injected an unescaped newline + stray backticks inside the string, then closed object early. Parser throws.

kevin: This smells like tokenization/kernel boundary cutting a UTF or escape sequence mid-token under quantization. We saw similar with interleaved kvprefix earlier. Is the canary using kvcache prefixing and streaming=true?

maria.l: Yes kvcache prefix enabled, streaming=true, batch=8, temp=0.2. Canary config link: https://redwood.internal/canaries/8231 (perm: eng-ml).

samir: Query I ran to compare fail rates (pseudo-SQL):
```
SELECT model, quant, streaming, count(*) as attempts,
  sum(case when parse_ok then 0 else 1 end) / count(*) as parse_fail_rate
FROM funcall_telemetry
WHERE canary_id = 8231
GROUP BY model, quant, streaming;
```
Results show parse_fail_rate for int8 streaming = 0.019, fp16 streaming = 0.006. Non-streaming int8 is 0.007 -> much closer.

kevin: Interesting — non-streaming is fine. So streaming + int8 + kvcache likely amplifies boundary truncation of escape sequences. Could be kernel-level token decoding changes in PTQ path that cause different chunk splits.

yasmin: Repro steps suggestion: 1) run canary with streaming=false. 2) run canary with kvcache_prefix disabled. 3) run with last-token padding (append spaces) to see if it stabilizes. Samir, can you schedule those three quick probes?

samir: On it. Running three probes now against a 1k sample from structured-output eval corpus (seeded, temp=0). Will post numbers in ~25m.

deploy-bot: Canary 8231 (raven-lite-v2 int8 PTQ) deployed to canary pool at 2026-03-20T14:02:00Z. Config: streaming=true, batch=8, kvcache=on.

eva: Also consider adding a transient parser-rescue in the client: try strict parse -> if fails, run a small regex-based "fix common escapes" pass (unescape newlines inside quoted values, close dangling quotes) then reparse. If that reduces observed failures by 70% we can keep canary while we root cause.

kevin: Agree. But we shouldn't hide severe corruption; keep telemetry tag 'rescue_attempted' and compare downstream correctness eval. We can add a config flag in the canary: structured_output.rescue: soft-wrapped. Example shim:```
if not parse(json):
  try -> repaired = json_repair_heuristic(raw_text)
  if parse(repaired): tag telemetry 'repaired_v1'
  else -> increment parse_hard_fail
```

maria.l: Quick decision: run the three probes (samir), enable rescue shim in canary but only on 10% sampling with telemetry tag, and schedule kernel-level trace on 1% of calls so runtime team can inspect chunk boundaries. If rescue drops fail rate <1% we keep canary; otherwise rollback to fp16. I'll run 1k smoke now.

samir: Probe 1 (streaming=false) done: parse_fail_rate = 0.62%. Probe 2 (kvcache off) done: 0.9%. Probe 3 (last-token padding + 3 spaces) done: 0.7%. Enabling rescue shim (10% sample) yields repaired_v1 hits ~0.9% and hard_fail 0.8%. Raw int8 streaming baseline was 1.9%.

maria.l: Thanks — rescue helps but doesn't fully close gap. Kernel tracing scheduled (kevin + eng-runtime). For now hold canary with rescue sampling enabled, set canary pass condition to require downstream eval (schema+semantics) stable at <1.2% parse+semantic failure across 10k examples. Rolling rollback if not met by EOD.

eva: Can we also run the deterministic eval with temp=0 and no streaming for 10k examples to get a clean quality baseline for model selection? If FP16 passes and int8 fails, we can promote FP16 fallback for funcall routes while keeping int8 for non-funcall APIs.

maria.l: Good plan. I'll queue the 10k run (temp=0, streaming=false) and post the job id.

kevin: Added a breakpoint trace in runtime: capture last 256 tokens pre-chunk and post-chunk, along with token ids and decoded text, for any call where repaired_v1 was triggered. That should show whether chunk boundary caused an escape to be split.

maria.l: Perfect. Thanks all — will update after 10k job completes and kernel traces land. :thumbsup:
